name: Guildism
summary: Guildism (guild socialism) holds that industry should be run democratically by the workers in each trade through national guilds, ending the wage system and capitalist profit, rent and interest. It rejects both private capitalism and bureaucratic state socialism, and replaces the all-powerful state with functional representation, with a coordinating Commune for consumers and citizens. Its adherents expected change through trade union action rather than a party seizing the state.
scope: The British guild socialist movement of about 1906-1923: S. G. Hobson and A. R. Orage's National Guilds (The New Age), and above all G. D. H. Cole's Guild Socialism Restated (1920) and the National Guilds League. Arthur Penty's medievalist craft strand is noted but not used for the core answers. Most modern statements are unaddressed by the movement and answered low.

keyFigures.name: G. D. H. Cole
keyFigures.role: Principal theorist and popularizer; founded the National Guilds League in 1915.

keyFigures.name: S. G. Hobson

sources.usedFor: Origins, Penty's medievalism, The New Age, thinkers and organisations.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not discussed as such; Cole's civic services run by a Commune budget imply public provision of health as a civic service.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Guildists want the wage system itself abolished, so a higher legal minimum is an inadequate palliative, though they would not oppose better pay.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Cole prefers negotiated Just Prices and a Commune financial pivot over market price-setting, though guilds still trade.

public-ownership.rationale: Guildists accept state or communal ownership of industry but only with the guilds holding control, so agreement is qualified.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Cole expects rent, interest and profit to be abolished and taxation levied at source on guilds; high taxes on the idle wealthy follow loosely.

unions-good.rationale: Hobson says the Trade Unions must be the driving force of the guild change, and Cole's guilds are unions transformed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Hobson calls for restoring the product to the producer and ends rent and interest, so property claims over capital are not fundamental.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Capitalist firms are meant to be replaced, not regulated, so the question's premise is largely bypassed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; guildists reject wage-slavery and want security of employment maintained, so cutting welfare is unlikely.

worker-ownership.rationale: Guilds hold control of industry for its workers, but Cole stresses public or communal title with workers' control, not worker ownership of firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Cole wants personal conduct regulated as little as possible and coercion as a last remedy; inferred libertarian stance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No guildist text addresses drugs; Cole's minimal regulation of conduct pulls one way, social-order concerns the other.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Hobson calls free speech, writing and publishing a cardinal matter; hate speech laws are not discussed.

strong-leader.rationale: Cole demands active democratic citizenship with recall and instruction of representatives, the opposite of leader-centred rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Cole says the omnicompetent State is unsuited to democracy and should wither, yet a coordinating Commune remains, so not an anarchist rejection.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; Cole hopes for a part-time citizen force, which cuts neither way clearly.

empower-police-military.rationale: Cole wants police appointed and controlled by wards and relies on social opinion over coercion.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No stated position; guild literature does not address it.

decide-locally.rationale: Cole's Wards and Commune with recall build power from small bodies, but guilds and national coordination also hold major powers.

rehabilitation.rationale: Cole calls coercion a last and desperate remedy; a rehabilitative approach is inferred, not stated.

traditional-family.rationale: Guildism has no doctrine on family; its medievalist wing leans traditional, Cole's socialist wing does not.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The movement predates the question; Cole favoured minimal regulation of conduct but adherents are unrecorded on this.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by guildists; no basis for inferring a position beyond Cole's minimal regulation of conduct.

more-religion-public.rationale: Cole wants churches independent of economic and civic power, though he sees spiritual life as important.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a guild concern; Cole's equality focus is economic, and positions on race are unrecorded.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources say nothing on gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cole wanted each country to work out its own path, but guildists emphasised craft and cultural councils over nationhood.

gradual-change.rationale: Cole urges evolutionary consolidation of forces, though he accepts a revolutionary element and does not respect existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration is not discussed; internationalism pulls against, trade-union protectionism pulls for.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Cole says guildists must be internationalists aiming at a federation of self-governing communities, inferred to favour some international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Cole has guilds handle foreign trade under Commune oversight, not open markets; not a stated free trade position.

nation-first.rationale: Cole says guildists like all socialists must be internationalists and seek a world of free societies.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's belief that real democracies cannot co-operate with tyrannies is not a case for intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Internationalism but no stated stance on borders; adherents unrecorded.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; Cole wants machinery applied fully to remove dirty work, but medievalists like Penty distrust industry.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the movement.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Cole wants fullest use of machinery for drudgery, but Penty opposed factory production; the movement is split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Cole says a revolutionary element is unavoidable and change may come with or without violence, though he prefers it to be a registration of accomplished facts.

experts-over-public.rationale: Cole wants active citizenship and control from below; each guild governs itself, not experts above them.

central-planning.rationale: Cole rejects the idea that the State can coordinate everything and builds on self-governing guilds with negotiated prices.

socialized-markets.rationale: Guilds trade at negotiated Just Prices and the Commune sets surpluses, a form of market among self-governing bodies.

land-value-tax.rationale: Cole wants communal appropriation of rent but does not propose a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not discussed; ending the private appropriation of rent and interest implies opposition to inherited unearned wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Hobson ties pay to function and abolishes wagery; an unconditional income is not part of guildism, though Cole expects equality to come gradually.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: No statement; guilds handle foreign trade but protection is not discussed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Cole puts credit and industrial banking inside the guild system and the Commune, not a state investment plan.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Cole accepts small socially useful cultivators and craftsmen, but the main means of production go to guilds.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Hobson wants the wage system abolished but guilds would still pay members; money remains, so the statement fits only half.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Cole puts the Commune in control of credit and currency, a public rather than market money system.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Guilds and Commune negotiate prices, but Cole denies the guilds are state-recognised employer bodies; he rejects employers entirely.

one-party-rule.rationale: Cole's democratic functional representation with recall rules out single-party rule, and he criticised Bolshevik bureaucracy as out of harmony with guild ideas.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; adherents were democrats but the monarchy was not a guildist issue.

democracy-best.rationale: Hobson states his unequivocal choice is for Democracy even at some cost to efficiency.

direct-votes.rationale: Cole favours direct election only where voters can meet and instruct their representative and prefers delegates with recall over referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Cole puts industrial democracy on the factory or workshop and a guild congress above it, but also keeps a Commune, so not councils instead of parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not discussed; adherents were federalists but no secession doctrine is recorded.

natural-rulers.rationale: Cole's functional democracy with recall and leaders chosen from below denies natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Cole says change may come with or without violence and expects a revolutionary element, so violence is not ruled out absolutely.

war-builds-character.rationale: Hobson condemns war profits as surplus value; no glorification of war is recorded.

separate-church-state.rationale: Cole says churches should remain independent of economic and civic power because spiritual freedom depends on it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Cole separates spiritual bodies from civic power; Christian guildists like Penty were medievalist, so some dissent exists.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Cole has judges appointed by the Commune and police by the wards, so these are public functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen force and internationalism; superiority is not a goal.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Cole's internationalism and federation of free communities do not use ethnicity as a basis; not directly discussed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Cole speaks of possessing and dispossessed classes and class-conscious workers but is not a historical materialist.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Cole says equality cannot and must not be a condition of the guild system but expects it to come gradually.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; Cole mentions colonies only as something the Commune handles while they exist.

civilizational-union.rationale: Cole's internationalism is a federation of self-governing communities, not civilization blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Guildists denounce profit and wage-slavery in favour of service and free association; Cole speaks of free association for service.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cole's guilds stress service but also individual liberty; no such formula is stated.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Guild writers never addressed nature's value; Penty's craft romanticism and Cole's machinery enthusiasm pull differently.

limit-population.rationale: Neither Cole nor Hobson wrote on population policy, and they blamed poverty on the wage system.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Penty's medievalism opposed factory production but Cole and Hobson wanted guilds applied to modern industry; the strand splits.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Cole welcomes machinery for drudgery but favours guild control, not disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: The movement predates the debate and gives no principle that decides it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Cole's core demand is self-government by participants, so rule by algorithms opposes this in principle.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Cole's wish to regulate personal conduct as little as possible.

restore-past-order.rationale: Penty sought a medieval-style restoration, Cole and Orage sought a modern reorganisation; the movement is split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Guildists held a definite doctrine about the wage system and industry rather than pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Cole calls trade union economic power, including direct action, the main tool for winning control of industry, while also using elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Cole starts workshop control inside the union to build the guild democracy, creating the new organs inside the old order.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Guildists want modern industry self-governed by workers; Penty's medievalism is craft, not foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Guilds are organised by industry and function; Cole keeps specialised guilds and functional representation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Cole expects equality to arise as payment for work done fades, but he does not set need as the rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Hobson's restoration of the product to the producer and the end of profit implies production for service, with consumers represented.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Hobson states profit is only possible by the power to buy labour as a commodity, which he treats as servitude.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Cole criticised Bolshevik bureaucratic tendency and wants democracy; he does not endorse class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Cole says socialism is compatible with large and small farming and distinguishes socially useful individual cultivators.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Hobson links war profits to surplus value but no doctrine of inevitable imperialist war is stated.

taxation-theft.rationale: Cole assigns the Commune taxation at source and finance as the pivot of the guild system.

harm-principle.rationale: Cole says personal conduct should be regulated as little as possible, which is near but is not a stated formula.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Guildism works with functional groups as the unit of representation.

conscription.rationale: Cole wants a part-time citizen force, not conscription, but mentions it little.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Hobson puts democracy first and Cole stresses active citizenship, so voice outranks exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Cole sees democratic citizenship, not customership, as the basis of public life and calls the omnicompetent State unsuitable.

positive-liberty.rationale: Hobson's economic emancipation from the wage system is a material condition of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not a guildist theme; Cole stresses economic over cultural power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not discussed; socialist egalitarian outlook implies rejection.

organic-representation.rationale: Cole holds that all true and democratic representation is functional representation, through trades and communities.

total-state.rationale: Cole says the State cannot coordinate everything and calls the omnicompetent State unsuitable to a democratic community.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not nationalist; Cole wants social reorganisation through guilds, not national regeneration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Internationalism and a federation of free societies oppose expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Cole's recall and instructed delegates are the opposite of personal oaths of lordship.

bound-labor.rationale: Hobson objects even to the wage system as servitude, so legally bound labour is the extreme opposite.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The guild texts contain no epistemology to draw on.

universal-morality.rationale: Not discussed in the sources read.

single-common-good.rationale: Cole's functional representation balances many interests rather than one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Guild socialists wrote nothing on Zionism, and Cole's internationalism offers no clear answer.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; Cole's federal internationalism gives no principle on diaspora citizenship.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed by guildists, who treated nationality as secondary to industrial organisation.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Cole wants democracy extended to industry with leaders chosen from below, and consumers represented in each industry.

school-vouchers.rationale: Cole makes education a civic service and wants teaching self-governing, not a voucher market.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Budget policy under capitalism was not a guildist concern since Cole's Commune sets the budget in a different system.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hobson defends civil liberties but sees wage servitude as unfreedom, rather than economic freedom as the base of political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Cole relies on social opinion over coercion but also on institutions of recall and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Cole says each country should work out its own social salvation yet seeks a federation, so self-rule without nationalist assertion.

force-without-un.rationale: Cole's internationalism implies scepticism of unilateral force; not stated.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Cole respects spiritual freedom of churches while medieval guilds had religious basis; no stated stance.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; internationalist outlook implies against.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; guild security of employment makes it moot.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hobson's wage system divides mankind into hateful segregations that guilds are meant to end; employers are replaced rather than partnered.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Penty and the medieval inspiration celebrate inheritance, and Cole supports cultural councils.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed, though Cole's internationalism might favour solidarity among peoples without a front against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Cole says guildists must be internationalists.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's democratic functional membership has no gender bar.

ban-interest.rationale: Cole's medieval guilds opposed usury and he ends interest as unearned income, though banking stays in guilds.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not discussed; egalitarian and internationalist principles oppose.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Cole sees the existing State as the political arm of the possessing class, to be superseded.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy goes unmentioned; Cole mentions mines only as a necessary monopoly to be run by a guild.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration was outside the movement's concerns, and internationalism pulls against forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial claim with no basis in guild thought.

proportional-representation.rationale: Cole rejects territorial parliament as a farce in favour of functional bodies, so party PR is not his answer.

national-mission.rationale: Cole's guildism is internationalist and federalist, with no mission to spread.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The guild texts read do not address women's position, though Cole's democratic ethos is egalitarian.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Cole criticises Parliament for replacing the represented with representatives.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not discussed; democratic socialist outlook opposes coercion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Cole wants wards to control police but says nothing on legal accountability for past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cole assigns the Commune finance, civic services, credit and war and peace, far beyond a night-watchman role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not discussed; internationalist and egalitarian ethos opposes.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Cole's democratic equality is stated in terms of citizenship, so equal worth is inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Cole says each country works out its own salvation; his internationalism is federation, not simultaneous revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement never addressed settler colonialism and mentions colonies only in passing.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law was outside the movement's scope; Cole keeps churches independent of the state.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Cole sees churches independent in spiritual matters; restriction not proposed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Cole views churches as independent; no stated school stance.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Cole expects the old State to wither and distrusts Soviet bureaucracy.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Hobson's choice for democracy and Cole's active citizenship imply authority by consent of those governed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade policy is not discussed; Cole assigns foreign trade to guilds under the Commune.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Cole accepts revolution with or without violence but not as aim; no principle of non-initiation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Hobson and Cole replace competition between employers with service and cooperation between guilds.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Hobson values freedom of speech and publication as cardinal; party bans not discussed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Hobson's wage-slavery critique treats dependence on an employer's power as unfreedom regardless of treatment.

separated-powers.rationale: Cole splits functions among guilds, Commune and civic bodies but does not follow liberal checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Cole builds change out of trade union action and the workers' industrial consciousness, not a vanguard party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: No statement; guilds aim at workers as a class but priority to the poor is not set.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed; Cole's communal ownership of rent runs against sale of homes, but small ownership is accepted.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Hobson defends industrial action and criticises treating strikes against the State differently from those against private employers.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Hobson and Cole locate poverty in the wage system and unearned incomes, not population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Cole uses election and recall within functional bodies, not lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Hobson stresses civil liberty and Cole treats coercion as last resort; emergency powers not discussed.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Cole's guild prices are negotiated to a Just Price and the Commune can fix prices above or below cost.

party-controls-media.rationale: Hobson calls the right to speak, write and publish a cardinal matter.

party-commands-army.rationale: Cole puts war power and any armed forces under the Commune with a citizen force, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the sources read.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Cole's recall and instructed delegates suggest representatives remain tied to those they represent; pay level not discussed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Cole binds delegates to those who chose them but parties are not his organ.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Cole's goal of a federation of self-governing communities supports pooling, though the EU came later.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Cole puts the power of war and armed forces in the Commune, not a head of state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Cole keeps churches independent and leaves their governance to them.

clerical-rule.rationale: Cole insists on churches independent of civic power and on democratic functional bodies.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Hobson denounces war profits but no revolutionary defeatism is recorded; the National Guilds League itself did not adopt it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Hobson's insistence on free publication and Cole's cultural councils imply opposition.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not discussed; recall and delegate model make it moot.

recall-officials.rationale: Cole makes ward representatives recallable by Ward Meetings and calls recall the key safeguard of indirect systems.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliances are not discussed; internationalism and wariness of war cut in different directions.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not discussed; Cole accepts the Commune's civic services and collective utilities, which may include housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen force under Commune control.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Penty's medievalism was craft-oriented but Cole and Hobson did not hold this.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not discussed; guildism had no national-question doctrine.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Cole wants teachers self-governing and values craft knowledge, but no anti-intellectual claim appears.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed by guild writers; internationalist egalitarian ethos suggests sympathy but nothing states it.

death-penalty.rationale: Cole sees coercion as last and desperate remedy; the death penalty is not discussed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum is not discussed; Cole makes education a civic service run by self-governing teachers.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; Cole treats education as a civic service run by self-governing teachers.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed; Cole prefers little regulation of conduct.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not discussed; internationalist outlook implies no.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language rights are not discussed in the guild texts.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's independent churches principle is about institutions, not exemptions from law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Cole holds personal conduct should be regulated as little as possible through opinion; no Mill-like claim.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt is not discussed in the sources read.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Cole holds that change is fundamentally economic and not political, an analogy to national independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; Cole prefers functional reorganisation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Hobson values civil liberty as a cardinal matter and prefers democracy even at some cost to efficiency.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not discussed; internationalism leans yes but no statement.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Cole has no head of state role in his Commune scheme.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Cole puts credit and currency under the Commune and the guild system, not an independent bank.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial disputes are not discussed in the guild texts.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Cole ends private appropriation of rent and treats property as held for communal service.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Cole criticised Soviet bureaucracy as out of harmony with guild ideas but did not call it capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; guildism has no environmental regulation doctrine.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances are not discussed; Cole's war and peace power sits with the Commune.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed in guild writing, which focused on industry.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Cole holds that churches should stay independent of civic and economic power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Cole's scheme has no head of state role, so the question gets no guidance.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not discussed; Cole gives the Commune war and peace powers without addressing secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not discussed, though Cole's federal design allows varied local forms under national coordination.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Cole's democratic functional society has no place for a sacred head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Cole taxes guilds at source and expects equality to grow; flat tax not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Hobson and Cole blame the wage system for servility, implying character is shaped by conditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Cole's democracy of recall and instructed delegates denies unbound rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and unrelated to guild concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Cole's design is functional democracy, not mixing few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Cole's delegates are recallable by those who elect them and his democracy opposes personal cults.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law was outside the movement's concerns.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Cole expects the guild system to end the possessing class, so a continuing class struggle is not anticipated; not discussed directly.

land-redistribution.rationale: Cole wants communal appropriation of rent and distinguishes capitalist farmers from socially useful cultivators; estates to farmers is not his scheme.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee questions were not discussed in the guild texts.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Cole says spiritual freedom depends on church independence from civic power.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not discussed; minimal regulation of conduct opposes.

common-currency.rationale: Cole puts currency under the Commune but nothing is said on shared currencies.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's internationalism is a federation of self-governing communities not defined by ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cole's cultural councils exist but are functional, not national.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration debates were outside the movement's scope.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cole says the needed change is fundamentally economic rather than political, but he is not a historical materialist.

ban-cartels.rationale: Cole calls monopoly a necessary evil even for a guild, implying some tolerance, but trusts are not specifically discussed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank rescues are not discussed; guilds treat credit as part of the guild organisation.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not discussed; Cole has judges appointed by the Commune.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not discussed; functional representation has no gender quota.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Cole has guilds handle foreign trade, implying openness; internationalism opposes bloc closure.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not discussed; internationalism and labour focus imply support for labour standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Cole expects equality to come as payment for work done fades and speaks of free association for service, a move toward service motives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Cole says revolution should register accomplished facts and a culmination of existing tendencies, not be created by a small group.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Ending rent and unearned income and a democratic functional order imply no hereditary privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Cole mentions colonies only as holdings that exist for now; tutelage is not endorsed.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not discussed; Cole treats education as a self-governing civic service and is internationalist.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-conscious policy was outside the movement's era and concerns.

public-money-creation.rationale: Cole has the Commune control credit and currency, and Orage-wing guildists backed social credit.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Cole expects the present situation to give way to change with or without violence and says capitalism is wage-slavery.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not discussed; Cole has guilds handling foreign trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not discussed; guildists see all wage workers as subject to the wage system.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from democratic equality and rejection of private economic power over others.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Hobson values civil liberties but guildism proposes no bill of rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts, which mention colonies only briefly.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hobson's unequivocal democracy and Cole's election and recall from below imply rulers are elected.

minority-veto.rationale: Cole's guild congress and Commune decide by representation and coordination, with no individual veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Cole's recall principle and willingness to see revolution imply the governed may remove rulers; constitutional resistance is not stated.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Cole criticises the sovereignty of Parliament and divides power between guilds and Commune.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred weakly from Cole's humane and egalitarian outlook.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use was not discussed by guildists.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Guildists seek workers' control, not charity from the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Cole demands active citizenship extended to industry as well as politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural theory of this kind appears nowhere in Cole or Hobson.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Cole sees the State as tied to the possessing class but does not describe a Gramscian consent mechanism.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-system theory is absent; Hobson's surplus value remark concerns wartime profit at home.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not discussed; democratic functional bodies would not use it.

party-own-road.rationale: Cole says each country should work out its social salvation for itself and on its own lines.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid was not discussed in the guild texts.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; movement faded before fascism's rise.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement ended before the totalitarianism debate.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not discussed; no basis to hold position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Cole's remark that countries follow their own lines is about socialism, not civilizational limits.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Cole puts war power and armed forces under the Commune and wants a citizen force.

paid-care-work.rationale: Domestic labour is not discussed in the sources read, though the abolition of wage-slavery is relevant by analogy.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations were not part of guild doctrine.

office-by-exam.rationale: Cole has leaders chosen from below within guilds; exam-based posts are not proposed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; guilds control their own industries but foreign ownership is not discussed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family law was not part of the guild programme.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Cole has Ward Meetings hold the right of recalling any ward representative and wants representatives instructed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not discussed; Cole wants security of employment maintained by unions and guilds, not private savings.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Cole wants private appropriation of rent replaced by communal appropriation while allowing socially useful cultivators to hold land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Cole's Commune sets the budget and taxation, not a territorial parliament.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed, though Cole wants communal appropriation of rent.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic civil rights doctrine not found in guild texts.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Penty's craft revival and Ruskin-style critique oppose shoddy mass goods; Cole's guild just price opposes shoddy work.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's federation of self-governing free societies and democratic internationalism oppose imposing control on an allied country.

corporate-influence.rationale: Cole's critique of capitalist power over the state implies agreement; lobbying not discussed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; the movement predates modern NGO funding debates.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not addressed by Cole or Hobson.

residents-only-property.rationale: Property purchase limits were not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Cole wants the insecurity of discontinuous employment removed, with unions maintaining the unemployed at their customary standard.

democratic-peace.rationale: Cole says between real democracies and tyrannies there can be no co-operation, but democratic peace is not stated.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Cole wants a democratic functional order obeyed by consent but does not discuss a general duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's internationalism does not settle it.

industrial-unions.rationale: Cole argues craft unionism cannot achieve control of industry and favours organisation by industry in guilds.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not discussed; no basis in guild thought.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not part of the guild programme.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from Cole's active citizenship and Hobson's cardinal liberty of publication; not stated.

local-production.rationale: Penty's medievalism and the local character of guilds favour local production; Cole's national guild scheme is less local.

informal-organisation.rationale: Guildism builds formal industrial organisations from the unions up, with congresses, communes and wards.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed; internationalist leanings are offset by Cole's emphasis on each nation's own path.

religious-nation.rationale: Cole keeps churches independent from civic power.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's federal internationalism of free societies opposes.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Cole's Commune pools finance as a pivot, but regional revenue sharing is not discussed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Cole accepts personal property and small cultivators while guilds control means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cole criticised Bolshevik bureaucracy but sought to co-exist and learn from Russia.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Cole places civic services under Commune bodies and utilities under a Collective Utilities Council.

religion-illusion.rationale: Cole acknowledges the religious basis of medieval guilds and spiritual freedom; no atheist doctrine.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Cole treats capitalism as wage-slavery to be superseded but not as historically useless; guilds apply machinery gained under it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred weakly from the claim that the wage system is the root of servitude; women's issues are not discussed.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts, though Cole's civic services might include it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaties are not discussed in the sources read.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cole's guilds are industrial and federal and not small communes, though the Commune is local.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Hobson presents guilds as an alternative to both state control and conventional trade unionism and to private capitalism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed; guildism had no connection.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not discussed; Cole prefers little regulation of conduct.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Hobson states his choice is democracy and defends free speech.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Cole keeps churches and civic power separate; not discussed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Cole mentions colonies as territorial questions only while they exist; exploitation is against wage-slavery critique.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not discussed; Cole separates churches and civic power.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Cole wants active citizenship in industry, wards and communes rather than passive consent.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic framework absent from the guild texts.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; guildism has no stated view.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Guildists placed themselves on the socialist side of the labour movement.

alienated-labor.rationale: Hobson's wage-slavery critique and Cole's call for control of the work process hold that wage labour is servile, though without Marxist alienation vocabulary.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not discussed; no basis in guild thought.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Cole derives authority from functional democratic representation.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not discussed, though Cole keeps churches independent of civic power.

social-market-economy.rationale: Cole seeks abolition of the wage system, not social protection of a market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Cole hopes for a part-time citizen force and does not abolish arms.

rich-first.rationale: Cole expects equality to come gradually, but he does not accept unequal growth as policy.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's internationalism does not decide bloc policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hobson's unequivocal democracy rejects hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Cole places credit and banking within the guild system; interest-free mutual banks are not specified.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International lending conditions are not discussed.

property-franchise.rationale: Hobson's democracy and Cole's active citizenship include workers; he distinguishes active and passive citizens by consumption, not property.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is absent from the guild texts.

reification.rationale: Hobson's treatment of labour as a commodity under the wage system is similar, but he does not state the Lukacs-style thesis.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Hobson treats freedom to publish as cardinal, warning even against unions blocking printing; wealth owning presses is not discussed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred weakly from Hobson's liberal civil liberties; legal theory is not discussed.

racial-franchise.rationale: Hobson's unequivocal democracy is against restricted franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; Cole's push for active citizenship points toward participation but internet tools could not be foreseen.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; transparency of public bodies is not discussed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not discussed; Cole prefers little regulation of conduct.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian ethos of guild socialism; never discussed.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's functional bodies replace sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Cole keeps churches independent of the state and says nothing on doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Cole argues that huge inequalities of wealth and power are fatal to real democracy.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; guild texts say nothing on this.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Cole holds that churches should stay independent of civic power and spiritual freedom matters.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Cole has wards appoint and control police and treats coercion as last remedy.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational design is absent from the guild texts.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Hobson wants structural change, not charity, and Cole has civic services publicly run.

term-limits.rationale: Cole's recall of officials is his mechanism; term limits are not discussed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Cole's instructed delegates and recall are related but not delegation of votes by policy area.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic concern not found in guild writing.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Cole leaves church affairs to the churches themselves.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not discussed; democratic ethos leans yes but unrecorded.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not discussed; Cole's active citizenship through the Ward could extend to residents but he does not say so.

rent-control.rationale: Cole opposes private appropriation of rent; capped rents are inferred, not stated.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not discussed, though guilds would control their trades and prices.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not discussed; democratic and civic ethos opposes.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; nuclear weapons did not exist in the movement's era.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the guild texts.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Hobson wants the product restored to the producer and objects to rent and interest as income from ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Cole accepts a citizen force and some violence; no pacifism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Hobson says Parliament neglects its spiritual duties and economic emancipation frees the religious spirit, but he does not frame politics as a struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Zionist questions are not discussed by guildists.

culture-before-state.rationale: Cole puts cultural councils into the guild scheme but does not treat culture as prior.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology is outside the movement's scope.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Theology is outside the movement's scope.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Not discussed; democratic and internationalist outlook opposes.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not discussed, though Cole's federal Commune could accommodate it.

independent-unions.rationale: Cole's guild congress succeeds the Trades Union Congress as a self-governing body, not a state organ.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Cole holds that socialism requires workers' control of industry from below and rejects State ownership as a substitute.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Cole has a Collective Utilities Council for local economic services, public in character.

second-chamber.rationale: Cole's scheme has guild congress and Commune bodies, a functional dual structure, but he rejects territorial parliament so a second chamber is a different idea.

municipal-property.rationale: Cole's Commune holds communal appropriation of rent and utilities, but industry belongs to guilds under public title, not the municipality.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Cole makes the Commune mainly a coordinating body rather than an administrative one, built from functional bodies.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed; Cole expects guild wages to move toward equality but says nothing of family needs.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anachronistic; Cole's Commune controls credit and currency but traceability is not discussed.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's era had no online life, and Cole wanted conduct regulated minimally.

person-over-state.rationale: Cole calls the omnicompetent State unsuitable to democracy and wants individuals to be active in self-government.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Hobson says economic emancipation will free the religious spirit and Parliament has spiritual duties; the framing is modest.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not discussed; Commune is a coordinating body with its own powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; genetic engineering lies far outside guild-era debates.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form is not discussed in the sources read.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Not discussed; functional representation is by trade, not race.

racial-pride.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Cole's internationalism and citizen force imply defence only; not stated.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts.

communal-electorates.rationale: Cole's representation is functional by industry and function, not religion or community.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not discussed in the guild texts.

free-public-college.rationale: Cole makes education a civic service and a self-governing profession; free tuition is inferred.

missingStatements.text: Industries should be run by the workers who work in them rather than by owners or the state.
missingStatements.rationale: Guild control of each industry by its workers, with consumers represented, is the defining demand of Cole and Hobson.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should be represented through their occupations and functions rather than only by territory.
missingStatements.rationale: Cole states that all true and democratic representation is functional representation.

notes: Penty's medievalist strand would answer more traditional on industrial and cultural questions; Orage added social credit pricing ideas. Many answers are low confidence because the movement addressed industry and the state, not social issues.
